siteTagline: In-depth loyalty-program hotel reviews across Southeast Asia
heroHeadline: Find your next *elite* stay across Southeast Asia

theme._note: Warm gold-on-charcoal palette for a luxury/points-traveler audience. Distinct from runsea.run's lime/black identity -- proves the token shape (not these values) is what the engine depends on.

_listicleConfig_note: minEntities lower than races (4) would let a 3-hotel guide through -- with several dozen hotels spread across 6 cities and one program, a category x city combo can be thin even when the city itself has good coverage.
_googleAnalyticsId_note: Not yet provisioned -- create a GA4 property for stayelite.travel and add its measurement ID here before launch (same step runsea.run went through).

sourceConfig._research_note: Hotels are evergreen (no lapsing) and the value here is review synthesis, not discovery -- researchPerRunLimit is set higher relative to entity count than races', and researchIntervalDays shorter, because sentiment/first-hand commentary IS the product for this vertical, not a supporting layer.
sourceConfig.discoveryConstraints: Only include hotels currently enrolled in Marriott Bonvoy (any Bonvoy-participating brand: Ritz-Carlton, St. Regis, W Hotels, JW Marriott, Marriott Hotels, Westin, Sheraton, Le Meridien, Renaissance, Autograph Collection, Courtyard, Four Points, etc.) located in one of the tracked cities. Do not include non-Bonvoy independent hotels, vacation rentals/serviced apartments, or hostels. If a source page mixes Bonvoy and non-Bonvoy properties, extract only the Bonvoy-enrolled ones.
sourceConfig._trustedAggregators_note: marriott.com's own destination/search pages are heavily client-rendered (same failure mode as World Athletics' calendar in the races instance -- a plain fetch returns navigation chrome and zero hotels), so discover-entities.js will need a text-rendering fetch strategy or a static per-city seed list rather than relying on these URLs directly. Kept here as the authoritative reference for manual research and for whichever fetch strategy discover-entities.js ends up using.

notes: Vertical instance config for 'hotels' (stayelite.travel). Launch scope: Marriott Bonvoy ONLY, across 6 Southeast Asian cities (Singapore, Bangkok, Phuket, Kuala Lumpur, Bali, Jakarta). Architecture is chain-agnostic by construction (same core-facts-registry pattern as every other vertical) -- adding World of Hyatt, Hilton Honors, or IHG One Rewards later means one new data/categories/*.json file plus real researched entities, never a template or route change. URL structure deliberately stays flat (/hotels/<slug>/, /categories/<slug>/, /regions/<slug>/) rather than nested /[program]/[city]/[slug] -- this is a brand-new domain with no indexed URLs to protect, and the flat model already gets 'add a chain without rebuilding' for free, matching how runsea.run works. The weekly refresh pipeline auto-commits directly to main when validation passes (an intentional deviation from the races instance's PR-only gate, at the site owner's request) -- see refresh workflow comments for the validation conditions that must pass before that happens.
